title: Why You Shouldn't Build a Business Alone

beats.say: If you're the smartest person on your team, the team is too small.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a solitary silhouette standing on a massive concrete bridge at blue hour against a heavy gray fog.

beats.say: Most solo founders try to play lawyer, accountant, and operator all at once.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of hands frantically moving papers on a dark wooden desk lit only by a single green banker's lamp.

beats.say: Why do independent builders burn out before reaching any real scale?
beats.visual: High angle shot of wet asphalt on an empty highway at night under the stark orange glare of sodium streetlights.

beats.say: You might assume doing every job yourself saves cash and keeps control.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary figure walking past massive industrial shipping containers under cold fluorescent security lights.

beats.say: Dan Peña argues you need a dream team of experts who are better than you.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a heavy steel warehouse door cracked open with a sliver of harsh white light cutting across the floor.

beats.say: Instead of grinding alone, he teaches you must surround yourself with elite operators.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a brass key turning slowly inside a heavy, dark iron deadbolt on an aged oak door.

beats.say: How do you actually pay for top-tier legal and financial talent when cash is tight?
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person leaning against a towering glass window pane while rain streaks down the outside in a sodium glow.

beats.say: Here's the honest catch: good people cost money or a share of your business.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of an empty concrete loading dock under a heavy gray sky with fog rolling across the tarmac.

beats.say: And his own business figures are self-reported, with no guarantees attached.
beats.visual: Low angle shot looking up at the sharp, brutalist edge of a concrete tower cutting into a cold dusk sky.

beats.say: Trade a slice of ownership for elite execution instead of hoarding zero percent.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of water droplets sliding down a cold, dark metal pipe under a single practical overhead bulb.

beats.say: Stop acting like a lone hero. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a single car driving across an open concrete overpass into the dim morning fog.

caption: If you try to do every job yourself, your business stays small. Trade equity for a real team. #money #personalfinance #businessmindset #wealthbuilding #entrepreneurship
description: Surround yourself with people better than you instead of doing every job alone. Learn the reality of building a dream team.
first_comment: What's the hardest part of delegating tasks in your work?

facts.claim: Dan Peña teaches building a dream team of lawyers, accountants, and operators.
facts.basis: Research brief: Dan Peña's 7 Steps to Super Success include creating a dream team.

facts.claim: His own business figures are self-reported.
facts.basis: Research brief: Most of his business numbers are his own claims: always say 'he says' or 'by his account'.

loop_map.stakes: Trying to run a business entirely alone without expert help.
loop_map.big_question: How do you actually pay for top-tier legal and financial talent when cash is tight?
loop_map.assume: Doing every job yourself saves cash and keeps total control.
loop_map.reveal: Good people cost money or a share of the business, and solo builders burn out.
